newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentines say joblessness biggest problem - poll.
newsitem.headline: Argentines say joblessness biggest problem - poll.

text.p: Unemployment is seen as the biggest problem facing Argentines living in the capital, according to a poll published Monday by daily La Nacion.
Sixty percent of the 805 Buenos Aires residents surveyed consider joblessness the country's top problem.
The national unemployment rate is currently 17.1 percent.

Meanwhile, only nine percent of respondents said they were happy with the free market economic policies of the government. Some 37 percent of those polled said the policies should continue with changes, while another 37 percent want a total change in economic policy.
The survey suggested 39 percent of respondents said their salaries were not high enough to get them through the month while 38 percent barely meet their costs.
Eighteen percent said they were economically "fine," but only four percent said they were able to save money.
The poll was carried out by Graciela Romer Associates between March 14 and March 25. No margin of error was given.
